title: Define compatibility flags and pinning granularity for new open-model intake
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: produce a clear, implementable spec for how new open/community model submissions are annotated with compatibility flags and how pinning granularity is applied at registration and runtime. This ticket reconciles PM needs (predictable behavior, clear rollback paths) with runtime constraints (kernel compatibility, KV cache expectations) and Design/Engineering constraints (console UX, API surface).

Scope: define the set of compatibility flags (semantic, tokenizer, kv-cache-behavior, streaming-safe, quantization-tolerance), describe pinning granularity (model-level, variant-level, endpoint-level), and specify the admission/rollback triggers and telemetry signals used to move variants between pin states. Deliverables: 1) acceptance criteria below, 2) compatibility flag definitions doc, 3) migration rules for existing unpinned variants, 4) a one-page Console UX mock and API contract for pin granularity.

Out of scope: engine-level kernel selection algorithms and quantization implementations (ENG will own those), full automation of rollouts (follow-up automation epic).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Compatibility flags enumerated and documented with machine-readable names and examples for 5 canonical failure modes (tokenizer mismatch, attention-op incompatibility, kv-cache hot-start mismatch, streaming chunk incompatibility, quantization error). 2) Pinning granularity options defined (MODEL, VARIANT, ROUTE) with examples showing how a route can override variant pinning. 3) API contract (POST /catalog/models with 'compat_flags' and 'pin_scope') and Console mock accepted by Design. 4) A telemetry gating plan listing 6 signals (error-rate, latency-p50/p95 delta, hallucination-rate on eval set, kernel-fallbacks, trace-sample incompatibility, tokenization errors) with thresholds that would cause automatic soft-pin or block. 5) Rollback rules documented: soft-pin -> notify + auto-fallback after 10% error increase for 30m; hard-pin removal requires a rollback PR and signoff from Eng + PM. 6) Migration plan for 1800 existing open variants with risk buckets and a dry-run subset identified. 7) Linked tickets created for Engineering implementation and Design assets.
notes: PM/ENG sync 2026-03-03: agreed to start with 6 canonical flags, add more later as signals appear (Aisha, Marco, Ellen)
Design review 2026-03-05: Console will show pin scope on model page and route override in rollout config (DES-2207)
Eng feasibility 2026-03-04: runtime can expose 'kv-cache-behavior' via probe; kernel incompatibilities require variant tagging from onboarding pipeline (ENG-4821)
Trade-off: wider default pinning reduces customer surprise but increases maintenance; proposed default = VARIANT pin for community weights, with ROUTE override

Linked artifacts: PRD draft https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MC/compatibility+flags+and+pinning, Google Drive spec https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-compat-spec, Console mockups https://drive.google.com/file/d/console-mock-031, Eval harness for gating https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/402
Telemetry dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/catalog-compatibility (sample panels for latency delta and tokenization errors)
Risk assessment: high for models with custom tokenizers; medium for large quantized variants; low for well-known community distributions with established CI
Next steps: final review with Security (if KMS/weights provenance required) and schedule ENG implementation tickets
